Alright, listen up. Sunday, November 22, 2026. Here’s what’s actually happening out there, no BS.

Money Talk

- **Social Security gets a bump, but the taxman cometh.**
  Good news, old timers: you're getting a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment in your Social Security checks for 2027. Bad news: Medicare and other tax changes might just claw some of that right back. The house always wins. [S3]
- **Google engineer living like a pauper to hit FIRE by 30.**
  This 26-year-old Google employee, raking in $323,000, is apparently living on less than minimum wage to hit $750,000 in investments in the next year. Respect the grind, but also, maybe enjoy a nice meal once in a while? The market isn't *that* forgiving. [S4]
- **Energy boss "hugely concerned" about winter bills.**
  Centrica CEO Chris O'Shea is "hugely concerned" that more people won't be able to pay their energy bills when prices jump next year. Guess those quarterly profits aren't quite softening the blow for the average consumer. [S7]
- **Trump eyes capping credit card interest and fees.**
  President Trump says he's open to working with Democrats to cap credit card interest and fees, claiming banks are making too much. A bipartisan attack on financial institutions? Now *that's* a hot take from left field. [S18]
- **Wellness industry cashing in on menopause.**
  Apparently, hot flashes and brain fog are the new gold rush. The wellness industry is cynically exploiting menopause symptoms, hawking everything from "lion's mane mushrooms" to "magnets for knickers." Hard to tell if it's innovation or just peak capitalism. [S13]

World Lore

- **Climate talks collapse over fossil fuels, again.**
  COP31 in Turkey ended exactly how everyone expected it would: with 200 countries failing to agree on a damn thing regarding fossil fuels, the primary driver of global warming. Because, you know, we *really* needed more gridlock on humanity's biggest challenge. [S22][S33][S34]
- **Trump and Xi embrace in Shenzhen.**
  President Trump's visit to China included a "bear hug" with Xi Jinping. The pundits are still trying to figure out what, if anything, Trump actually got out of it. Probably a good photo op, knowing him. [S23]
- **Pentagon tells Canada to "get serious" about defense.**
  Ouch. The Pentagon issued a sharply worded fact sheet accusing Canada of being a less-than-credible partner due to its military readiness and low defense spending. Guess the maple syrup shield isn't cutting it for NORAD anymore. [S16]
- **Suspected drone hits Russian ship in Libyan port.**
  A Russian vessel got dinged by what's believed to be a drone strike in Benghazi, Libya. Just another Tuesday in the Mediterranean, but definitely raises the temperature in an already boiling region. [S31]
- **Lebanese villagers return to destroyed homes.**
  As Israeli forces pull back from southern Lebanon, villagers are returning to find their homes wrecked. It's a stark reminder of the human cost of conflict, even when the headlines move on. [S21][S25]

Tech Tea

- **DNI warns of holiday tech "bumps in the road."**
  Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton is bracing Americans for more tech outages ahead of Thanksgiving travel, after recent disruptions to air travel, Microsoft 365, and banking. So, add "system collapse" to your holiday travel anxieties. [S2]
- **AI's 2027 reckoning: Cyberattacks as a constant.**
  Experts are unanimously predicting that 2027 will be the year cyberattacks, driven by increasingly sophisticated AI, become a "constant" threat to businesses and critical infrastructure. Get ready to live in the digital equivalent of Mad Max, apparently. [S17]
- **Signal blocks screenshots to fight AI surveillance.**
  Signal is clamping down on mobile screenshots on both Android and iOS, calling AI surveillance an "existential threat." This is either a brilliant move for privacy or a tacit admission that AI has already won the spy game. [S43]
- **Banks are kicking out your AI agents.**
  Major US financial institutions are officially banning third-party AI bots from logging into your accounts, warning that any bot-caused mistakes are on *you*. Your robo-financial advisor just got served. [S54]
- **Game dev pulls AI music after player backlash.**
  The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus got review-bombed on Steam after players discovered AI-generated music in the game. The developer quickly removed it. Looks like the gaming community isn't ready for their soundtracks to be written by algorithms. [S47]

Creator Szn

- **GTA VI just dropped, say goodbye to productivity.**
  Grand Theft Auto VI is out, and millions have already checked out of reality. It's not just a game; it's a global cultural event and a masterclass in how to capture attention in the digital age. [S14]
- **AI music gets an immediate delete from a popular game.**
  When fans discovered AI-generated music in the new Binding of Isaac expansion, they review-bombed it so hard the dev pulled the tracks. Turns out, "digital culture" sometimes prefers human-made art, even in a hyper-digital world. [S47]
- **Sheherazaad's "genre-chaotic" debut LP hits the airwaves.**
  Singer Sheherazaad, already making waves with her previous EP, just dropped "Khudgarzi," a reverb-drenched, "genre-chaotic" folk-noir album primarily sung in Urdu. Another win for unique voices cutting through the noise. [S49]

Supply Lines

- **DHL Express launches AI for customs clearance.**
  DHL Express is rolling out a new AI-generated product identifier to simplify customs clearance for small cross-border shippers in the U.S. Less paperwork, more packages moving – good for everyone, especially for SMEs trying to play in the global market. [S59][S65][S67]
- **FedEx expands European footprint with Polish acquisition.**
  FedEx, alongside private equity partners, just acquired a Polish logistics company. Smart move to deepen its presence in Eastern Europe, a key hub for manufacturing and distribution. [S70]
- **Amazon dives deeper into same-day prepared meal delivery.**
  Amazon is expanding same-day delivery of prepared meals across 2,300 cities. This isn't just about groceries; it's a direct shot at local restaurants and traditional food delivery apps, leveraging their last-mile supremacy. [S75]
- **LA-Long Beach port strike narrowly averted with tentative deal.**
  A tentative union accord means the immediate threat of a strike at the nation's busiest port complex has been eased. Huge sigh of relief for anyone dealing with ocean freight, as a shutdown there would have been a catastrophic choke point. [S58]
- **Mexican truckers secure safety agreements after strike.**
  Mexican trucking organizations struck 29 agreements with the government to improve highway safety and freight conditions following a nationwide strike. It's a win for drivers, and hopefully means fewer disruptions and safer transit for goods coming across the border. [S56]
- **Ocean freight rates dip, but charter rates climb.**
  Here's a head-scratcher: ocean freight spot rates are cooling on some major trades, yet containership charter rates are still climbing. It suggests carriers are still seeing underlying demand or are very good at managing capacity to keep their ships busy. [S62]

Speed Round

- DNI warns of pre-Thanksgiving tech outages, so maybe charge your devices.
- Trump wants to cap credit card fees, making banks nervous.
- COP31 climate talks on fossil fuels? Hard pass, apparently.
- Signal is blocking screenshots, escalating the privacy war against AI surveillance.
- Gaming community says "nah" to AI-generated music in new releases.
- The Pentagon just told Canada their military isn't credible. Oof.
- Grand Theft Auto VI is out, and yes, your friends are already gone.
